passage:
Looking back, my anger was the loudest thing in the room that week. A "recruiter" had taken a registration fee for a job that did not exist, and when I understood, I shook with rage. I wanted to track the person down and make them suffer.

My cousin Vishal took the phone gently out of my hand. "That could go wrong in ways you can't see. Use that energy on the complaint."

So I did. I saved screenshots of the chats, the phone number and the transaction IDs, told my bank, and filed a report on the cyber portal. Then I posted a warning in my college alumni group.

The anger did not vanish, but it had a job now. Two friends wrote back to say they had seen messages from the same recruiter.

Rajni

qa.q: What did the fake recruiter take from Rajni?
qa.a: The recruiter took a registration fee for a job that did not exist.

qa.q: What did Rajni want to do at first, and what does it show?
qa.a: Rajni wanted to track the person down and make them suffer, which shows intense rage.

qa.q: How could Rajni's anger be put to use?
qa.a: By saving screenshots, the phone number and transaction IDs, telling the bank, filing on the cyber portal, and warning friends.

qa.q: Why might Vishal have taken the phone out of Rajni's hand?
qa.a: Vishal worried that going after the scammer could go wrong in ways Rajni could not see, and wanted the energy to go into the complaint.

grounding: Rajni's rage at a fraudster is channelled into a proper complaint with screenshots and transaction IDs and a warning to friends, not a personal hunt.

passage:
The power was out across Tejas's colony in Nagpur, his phone at twelve per cent, when he realised the "buyer" for his old laptop had sent a fake payment screenshot. The laptop was already gone with the courier. Tejas punched the pillow, jaw clenched.
His friend Anirban, sitting in the dark with him, said, "I know a guy who can trace the number. We'll go to his house and get it back."
Tejas was tempted. The rage felt like fuel.
"No," he said finally. "That's how people get hurt." He used the last of the battery wisely: screenshots of the chat, the fake payment, the courier receipt, the buyer's number. Then he typed out the complaint on the cybercrime portal and filed it before the phone died.
The next morning, with the power back, he posted a warning in his college group with the buyer's number. Three friends replied: the same person had tried them.

qa.q: What had the buyer sent Tejas?
What was Tejas feeling when he realised he'd been scammed?
qa.a: He felt furious, punching the pillow with his jaw clenched, and tempted by the idea of hunting the scammer down.

qa.q: How did Tejas channel his anger usefully?
qa.a: He saved screenshots, the courier receipt and the number, filed a complaint on the cybercrime portal, and warned friends in his college group.

qa.q: How might Anirban see Tejas's refusal to go after the scammer?
qa.a: Anirban may feel a bit let down at first, but likely sees that Tejas chose a safer and more useful path.

grounding: The protagonist is enraged at a fraudster but channels it into a proper complaint with evidence and warning friends, rather than hunting the scammer.

passage:
Sumit found out on a Tuesday that the "part-time job" of rating hotels online had been a scam. He had paid three deposits to unlock "higher tasks", and now the group admins had blocked him. His ears rang with anger.
His flatmate Zeenat found him drafting messages to the scammer's number, full of threats, and searching for ways to find the person's address. "What are you doing?"
"Getting my money back. Or at least scaring them."
Zeenat sat down. "They do this to thousands of people. You won't scare them. You'll just give them more of your details."
Sumit stared at the screen. His hands were shaking. Then he deleted the threats.
Together they collected everything: the group screenshots, the UPI transaction IDs, the admins' numbers. He called the cybercrime helpline, then filed a complaint on the portal. That night he messaged his cousins and two college groups: "If anyone offers you money to rate hotels, it's a scam."

qa.q: How many deposits had Sumit paid to unlock higher tasks?
What was Sumit feeling when Zeenat found him?
qa.a: He felt furious, his ears ringing and hands shaking, wanting to threaten the scammer and track them down.

qa.q: What did Sumit do instead of retaliating?
qa.a: He deleted the threats, collected screenshots and transaction IDs, called the cybercrime helpline, filed a complaint, and warned his cousins and friends.

qa.q: How might Zeenat see Sumit's threats?
qa.a: Zeenat sees them as risky and useless, worried they would only expose more of Sumit's details.

grounding: Enraged at a fraudster, the protagonist is tempted to threaten and hunt them, but gathers evidence, files a proper complaint and warns friends.
